title: Hours remain more stable than earnings, but the direction pattern changes across children and SNAP contexts
source_unit: identified 2025 SIPP person, resource band at month t to direction of valid earnings/hours at month t+1, grouped by children and SNAP receipt at month t

observations.period: 2024 reference year; monthly direction by resource band; children present at month t

denominator.unit: valid earnings person-month pairs; hours direction uses its own 2,859-pair universe and each resource band has its own denominator

earnings_direction_by_resource_band.unit: percent; direction categories with Fay-BRR standard errors in percentage points, ordered increase/decrease/same

hours_direction_by_resource_band.unit: percent; direction categories with Fay-BRR standard errors in percentage points, ordered increase/decrease/same

observations.method: Same-person monthly cross-lag from THINCPOV at month t to direction of nonnegative numeric TPEARN and TMWKHRS at month t+1, grouped by RHNUMU18 > 0; first-month WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Census Fay BRR, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Earnings and hours use separate valid pair universes and each resource-band cell has its own denominator. Directional estimates are descriptive; children present is a household composition marker, not a care event or causal exposure. Approximate intervals are design-based Fay-BRR intervals.
observations.subgroup: SIPP person-month pairs with at least one child under 18 at month t; resource bands are THINCPOV categories.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable hours can coexist with changing pay, schedule quality, unpaid care, or household substitution. Higher earnings movement at higher resources does not establish improved security or greater control.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; monthly direction by resource band; no children present at month t

denominator.unit: valid earnings person-month pairs; hours direction uses its own 3,565-pair universe and each resource band has its own denominator

earnings_direction_by_resource_band.unit: percent; direction categories with Fay-BRR standard errors in percentage points, ordered increase/decrease/same

hours_direction_by_resource_band.unit: percent; direction categories with Fay-BRR standard errors in percentage points, ordered increase/decrease/same

observations.method: Same-person monthly cross-lag as the children-present observation, grouped by RHNUMU18 = 0.
observations.uncertainty: Earnings and hours use separate valid pair universes; no household weight or causal adjustment is used. Children absent is not proof of no caregiving responsibility.
observations.subgroup: SIPP person-month pairs with no child under 18 recorded at month t; resource bands are THINCPOV categories.
observations.counterinterpretation: A larger same-earnings share in the lowest-resource cell can reflect measurement, composition, or constrained job movement; it is not evidence of stability or welfare.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; monthly direction by resource band; SNAP receipt at month t

denominator.unit: valid earnings person-month pairs; hours direction uses its own 1,167-pair universe and each resource band has its own denominator

earnings_direction_by_resource_band.unit: percent; direction categories with Fay-BRR standard errors in percentage points, ordered increase/decrease/same

hours_direction_by_resource_band.unit: percent; direction categories with Fay-BRR standard errors in percentage points, ordered increase/decrease/same

observations.method: Same-person monthly cross-lag as the children-present observation, grouped by RSNAP_MNYN = 1.
observations.uncertainty: SNAP receipt is a reported program-status marker, not benefit adequacy or a causal treatment. Earnings and hours have separate universes and the lower-resource cells are smaller.
observations.subgroup: SIPP person-month pairs reporting SNAP receipt at month t; resource bands are THINCPOV categories.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher earnings decreases than increases in the highest SNAP/resource cell do not identify loss, and stable hours do not identify stable household room.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; monthly direction by resource band; no SNAP receipt at month t

denominator.unit: valid earnings person-month pairs; hours direction uses its own 5,257-pair universe and each resource band has its own denominator

earnings_direction_by_resource_band.unit: percent; direction categories with Fay-BRR standard errors in percentage points, ordered increase/decrease/same

hours_direction_by_resource_band.unit: percent; direction categories with Fay-BRR standard errors in percentage points, ordered increase/decrease/same

observations.method: Same-person monthly cross-lag as the children-present observation, grouped by RSNAP_MNYN = 2.
observations.uncertainty: No SNAP receipt is a reported program-status marker, not absence of need. Earnings and hours have separate universes and no household weight or causal adjustment.
observations.subgroup: SIPP person-month pairs reporting no SNAP receipt at month t; resource bands are THINCPOV categories.
observations.counterinterpretation: The contrast with SNAP recipients may reflect eligibility, income, household composition, work, or selection; it does not estimate a SNAP effect.

related_sources.claim: The related synthesis defines the directional work, tenure, care, and hardship boundaries and the need for subgroup conditioning.

boundary: This is a descriptive same-person monthly directional cross-lag, not a causal or household-weighted estimate. Children and SNAP status are month-t conditioning markers; they do not identify a care event, benefit effect, desired hours, job quality, remedy, trust, political action, or exit. Earnings and hours retain separate valid pair universes and all resource-band denominators are cell-specific.
